titulo: Golden set: evals for your agent
lead: You changed the prompt, swapped the model, installed a skill: did the agent get better or just different? A golden set is a frozen list of real cases with the right answer, checked by code, that you run on every change. In this lesson you build one, compare two versions, and see a regression hidden behind the same total.
objetivo: build a golden set with real cases, grading by code, and a comparison with the previous version that flags regressions.

aprende.t: The case format: id, category, input, expected, source
The three kinds of grader: code, model, and person
Scoreboard by category and case-by-case regression
When the set got too easy

hero_alt: Open steel drawer with sample cards and reference pieces in compartments.

secoes.titulo: From the real error to the regression verdict

nos.detalhe: The best cases come from errors that already happened: the issue the agent classified wrong, the answer a customer complained about. Each one goes in with its source noted.
id, category, input, what is expected, and where it came from. Frozen with a date: changing a case means changing the ruler, and that is recorded as a new version of the set.
rodar-evals.py sends prompt + case through stdin to any command: the fake agent in the rehearsal, claude -p or codex exec in the real run. Same suite, different engines.
The answer is JSON and each field is compared with the expected value. No model judge when code can check it: it is cheaper, it does not drift, and it has no opinion.

Total per category and, with --base, the comparison with the previous version: the case that passed in every attempt and now fails is a REGRESSÃO, and the script exits with 1. An equal total can hide a swap.

secoes.volta: A new failure becomes a new case in the set
secoes.legenda: Code-based grader first; model-based only for what is subjective (lesson 6); human-based to calibrate both.

secoes.sub: From the sources: Anthropic (agent evals), LOOP-R and the FEC track.

texto: By code (tests, static analysis, checking tool calls), by model (rubric, pairwise comparison, multiple judges) and by person.
The model-based grader has to be calibrated with human labels before it counts.
LOOP-R asks for 20 to 50 cases per artifact eval and treats fewer than 30 observations as a weak signal.
The rehearsal uses 10 cases to fit on the screen; yours starts with 20.
The FEC track's set has a set id, a freeze date, and for each case: id, question, expected facts and category.
In the 05/02/2026 version it announces 30 cases and has 3 filled in: a good structure is not a finished set. Count the lines before trusting the score.

secoes.titulo: The set and the rehearsal agent
secoes.sub: An issue triage agent: it returns the type (bug, request, question) and whether it is urgent. The 10 cases are examples written for the course.

blocos.conteudo:
You triage issues for a web system. Read the issue at the end and classify it.

tipo: "bug" (something broken), "pedido" (new feature) or "duvida" (usage question).
urgente: true only if the system is down, money or data is being lost, or there is a security flaw.

Answer with a single line of JSON only, nothing else:
{"tipo": "bug", "urgente": false}

E=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-verificacao-v72/kit/evals; mkdir -p /tmp/ensaio-evals
A="python3 $E/agente-triagem-falso.py"
TRIAGEM_VERSAO=1 python3 $E/rodar-evals.py --agente "$A" --saida /tmp/ensaio-evals/v1.tsv; echo "saída: $?"
TRIAGEM_VERSAO=2 python3 $E/rodar-evals.py --agente "$A" --saida /tmp/ensaio-evals/v2.tsv \
  --base /tmp/ensaio-evals/v1.tsv; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
armadilha  0/1
bug        5/5
duvida     2/2
pedido     2/2
total      9/10 (90%)  → /tmp/ensaio-evals/v1.tsv
saída: 0
armadilha  1/1
bug        5/5
duvida     2/2
pedido     1/2
total      9/10 (90%)  → /tmp/ensaio-evals/v2.tsv
MELHOROU  t07
REGRESSÃO t06 (passava em v1.tsv)
1 regressão(ões): não promova
saída: 1

Both versions score 9/10. Version 2 fixed the trap (t07) and broke a request (t06, which ends in "?" and turned into a question). The total alone would say "tie".

abas.rot: Common mistake: looking only at the total
abas.html: An aggregate score hides a swap: one case gets better, another gets worse, and the number stays the same. Compare case by case with the previous version and treat any regression as a block, even when the total goes up.

secoes.titulo: The same set with the real agent
secoes.sub: Uses your subscription quota: 10 calls. Each call is a claude -p with no tools.

blocos.rot: Terminal · real (continues from the previous block)
blocos.conteudo:
python3 $E/rodar-evals.py --agente 'claude -p --tools ""' --saida /tmp/ensaio-evals/real.tsv \
  --base /tmp/ensaio-evals/v1.tsv; echo "saída: $?"
# ou: --agente 'codex exec -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -'
wc -l < /tmp/ensaio-evals/real.tsv

abas.html:
armadilha  1/1
bug        5/5
duvida     2/2
pedido     2/2
total      10/10 (100%)  → /tmp/ensaio-evals/real.tsv
MELHOROU  t07
sem regressão
saída: 0
11

Claude Code 2.1.303, the subscription's default model, 1 min 19 s for the 10 cases. The model's score may change on your machine; the file with 11 lines (header + 10) will not.

A set that the agent gets entirely right does not separate the good version from the bad one: any change will score 100%. When that happens, add harder cases (the real traps, the ambiguous inputs) until the score has room to be wrong again.

secoes.sub: Rehearsal, real run and your agent's set.

exercicios.texto: Run the rehearsal for both versions.
exercicios.pronto: v1 prints total 9/10 (90%) and saída: 0; v2 prints REGRESSÃO t06 (passava em v1.tsv) and saída: 1.

exercicios.titulo: E14 · The same set with the model
exercicios.texto: Run the real block with claude -p or codex exec.
exercicios.pronto: the command ends with a total line and wc -l < /tmp/ensaio-evals/real.tsv → 11.

exercicios.texto: Choose an agent or prompt of your own with output you can check. Write 20 cases in the casos.jsonl format, starting with the failures you have already seen, and a prompt that asks for JSON. Run the current version as a baseline.
exercicios.pronto: wc -l < [seus casos].jsonl → 20 or more, and python3 $E/rodar-evals.py --agente "[seu agente]" --casos [seus casos].jsonl --prompt [seu prompt] --saida base.tsv prints the total line with less than 100%.

perguntas.p: Version 2 has the same total as version 1. What does rodar-evals.py say?
opcoes: A tie, you can promote it
Nothing, because the total is the same
perguntas.explica: The comparison is case by case: t06 used to pass and now fails. A regression blocks the promotion even when the total is equal or higher.

perguntas.p: When should you use a code-based grader instead of a model judge?
opcoes: Whenever the answer can be checked field by field or by a test
Only when the model is down
perguntas.explica: Code doesn't drift, has no length bias, and doesn't use your subscription quota. Keep the model judge for what is subjective, and only after it has been calibrated.

perguntas.p: The real agent got 10 out of 10. What do you do with the set?
opcoes: Add harder cases until there is room to fail again
perguntas.explica: A saturated set can't tell versions apart. Harder cases and real traps give you back the power to compare.

perguntas.p: Where do the best cases for a golden set come from?
opcoes: From the model, which generates examples
From real failures that already happened, with the origin noted
perguntas.explica: A real failure is the case you need to make sure never comes back. Each case carries its origin so someone knows why it exists.

itens.texto: One JSON line per case, with the expected result and origin; changing a case means a new version of the ruler.
Ask for JSON and check it field by field; use a model judge only for the subjective.
Compare case by case with the previous version; an equal total can hide a swap.
